refutations.property: An error result leaves the association failed.
refutations.input: abstract state: host association identity = `0`; errors associated with demand polling observations = `[0]`; lane indices associated with demand observations = `[0]`; per-element results of `self.demand.try_next_lane() = [1]`; association status when failure recording is attempted = `[1]`; error carried by the association status during failure recording = `[0]`; per-lane availability state = `[true, true]`; converted control-ring error identities = `[0]`; per-element results of `self.association.ended() = [0]`; errors associated with post-demand ending observations = `[0]`; per-element results of `self.association.ended() = [0]`; errors associated with pre-demand ending observations = `[0]`; demand-wait error = `[7]`; per-element results of `let Err(error) = self.demand.wait_for_demand(wake_count) = [true]`
refutations.sketch: If both calls to self.association.ended() observe a live association, demand polling reports Satisfied, and the demand wait returns an error, the error path would invoke failure reporting. If the association becomes peer-closed before failure recording, matches!(*status, HostAssociationStatus::Live) is false, so the wait error would be returned without being recorded as the association failure. This conditionally refutes the expectation that every demand-wait failure returned by next_lane is also recorded on the association.
